test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 1 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A sum of ₹36,000 deposited at a certain rate of compound interest, compounded annually, becomes three times itself after 6 years. How much will it become after 18 years at the same rate of compound interest?
solution:
Given:

Amount Three times under compound interest in 6 years.

Concept used:

Amount = Principal × [{1 +{ r over 100}}]^n

r = rate of interest

n = time in years

Calculation:

From the given data, we know that the amount doubles

Let us consider,

Amount = 3P

Principal = P

Substitute the values in the formula

3P = P × [{1 +{ r over 100}}]⁶

3 = [{1 +{ r over 100}}]⁶

We know that 3³ = 27

So, take power as 3 on both the sides

3³ = [[{1 +{ r over 100}}]⁶]³

27 = [[{1 +{ r over 100}}]¹⁸] ----- (1)

Compare equation (1) with the formula

So amount will be 27 times of principle in 18 years, so 27 × 36000 = 972000.

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**
